text.p: Bulgaria's 1996 Gross Domestic Product fell by a real 10.9 percent levs compared to a 2.5 percent growth in 1995, the National Statistics Institute (NSI) said on Thursday.
A further fall by a real three to five percent was expected this year, the NSI said in a statement.

The lev fall in 1996, shrinking demand and drastic fall in purchasing power due to mismanagement by former Socialist government and delayed structural reform made Bulgaria a laggard among former East Bloc economies last year, the NSI said.
The GDP stood at 1,660.2 billion levs at current prices last year compared to 852 billion levs in 1995, NSI figures showed.
In dollar terms GDP stood at $9.24 billion last year or $1,128 per capita. @
"The drastic fall of GDP last year has made 1996 one of most grim in economic terms since Bulgaria began its transition to market economy," the NSI said.
Gross Domestic Product fell a real 22.6 percent between 1990 and 1996, NSI said. Private sector share in GDP fell to 47.4 percent last year from 48.1 percent in 1995.
The slump in GDP in 1996 has set an extremely negative basis for economic development this year although the business climate has begun to improve in the first quarter, the NSI said. @
Business managers polled by the NSI expected a rise in economic activity in 1997 but economic recovery would be accompanied by growth in unemployment.
A NSI survey showed that state enterprises operated at 63 percent of their capacity and private ones at 65 percent at the beginning of April.
The NSI projection of a fall in GDP by three to five percent this year compared to projections of a fall of 4.8 percent by the International Monetary Fund. @

Economy Institute at the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences has projected a fall of 5.5 percent while the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development expected a six percent fall. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
